Use WP-31 LiveKit adapter and WP-32 participant snapshot; recheck policy/consent immediately before external start and stop on policy change under ratified semantics. Consume verified WP-32 webhook authentication boundary; scope known egress binding to workspace/provider/account and durable provider event ID; reconcile independently with provider/object metadata. Use foundation job leases with fencing token, bounded attempts/backoff/DLQ and policy recheck at claim/write/publish. Process only finalized input checksum. Reconcile output after crash before rewriting; publish recording.preview_ready exactly once for successful current job. Lease expiry recovers killed worker; old lease cannot commit. Preview job never writes transcript ready or promotes unfinished raw media.

Pinned sandboxed ffmpeg/ffprobe adapter with fixed args and validated input/output paths, CPU/memory/wall-time/output-size limits, restricted protocols/no network egress and sanitized failure classes. Validate decodability/codec/duration before WP-39 finalization; hostile/truncated input times out or quarantines. An executable must supply this behavior, not an echo/mock URL.

Add immutable consent/version/participant evidence, egress uniqueness, recording-to-WP-39 file/object association, artifact checksum/size/codec/retention label and unique preview job key using accepted common tables and composite workspace/entity identity. risks: The shared calls/contracts.ts, commands.ts and repository.ts names are repeated across WP-31/32/33/34. Treat them as one owned integration area, not independently creatable files after predecessors land.

Actual inspected sources may change during root wave0 integration; dispatched input HEAD and whole-file content hashes are different forms of evidence. Refresh changed files, not silently reuse stale line numbers.

Public StartRecording payload consentVersion:string/consentingPrincipalIds differs from domain StartCallRecording consentRevision:number; recordingRef/result lifecycle also needs accepted canonical-result mapping. Avoid parallel or permissive schemas.

StopRecording and GetPreview are required by apiChanges but lack full normative secondary schemas; provider callback authenticity and unknown-egress/account scope must be supplied by accepted WP-32 contracts.
rooms currently disabled; setting provider decided/recordingConsent:true or marking a native journal completed is not genuine recording evidence.

Supplied grants are forgeable at the boundary absent server authority; pure expiry helper only checks expiry when action.now is supplied. Capture call currently omits now. Replace shared authorization, do not special-case a failing actor.

Crash after external egress/object success before receipt is ambiguous; naive retries create duplicate effects or accessible orphan objects. Stable refs, reconciliation, unique keys and fenced publication all required.

Signed URL expiry alone does not ensure immediate revoke/deleted-key denial through CDN/cache. Accepted WP-39 access/key/asset-host semantics must demonstrate old URL failure and current policy, without claiming deletion of external copies.
ffmpeg CPU/wall/memory/protocol/output limits and codec/build license must be actually enforceable and audited; process timeout alone may leave children or unsafe network protocols.

Participant recording revoke/stop/redaction semantics, media tolerance, retry/resource bounds and retention source-removal SLA are not numeric/fully defined in inspected WP-33 specification. Root must ratify them; preflight does not weaken criteria.

Full summary/search/agent source invalidation involves downstream WP-34 and provenance WP-50; startup must not wait on WP-34/47 (would cycle), but full integrated acceptance cannot be called N/A or complete before those behaviors are observed.
Preserve usable standalone device/local Whisper/audio/import/recovery pipeline and require separate upload/cloud-send consent; no new recording store/surface and no automatic local media upload.
Generic mentions/notifications/agent access are mandatory completeness items with integration-owner contracts still missing in scoped code; lack of implementation is not a reason to mark them N/A.
